question.text: Which of the following best describes the 'carried interest' earned by an AIF investment manager?

answer.text: Additional returns paid to the investment manager as an incentive to outperform the hurdle/preferred return, allocated within the waterfall after investor corpus/preferred return in some structures

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook describes carried interest/carry as additional returns paid to the investment manager as an incentive to outperform the hurdle/preferred return. The 2-20 model is referenced as a developed-market custom, and in some waterfall structures carry comes after investor corpus and preferred return. The Trap: Carry is performance-linked, not a salary, deposit interest, or borrowing cost. It is triggered only when fund returns exceed the hurdle. Note: Earlier wording framed 20% carry as the typical Indian-market figure, called carry the manager's "main motivation," and treated prior carry as a proven track-record signal. The checked workbook qualifies that additional returns and the 2-20 model are not standard features in the evolving Indian AIF market, so those claims have been removed and replaced with the hurdle/waterfall framing.
